label: Acts 6:1
text: Now in those days, when the number of the disciples was multiplying, a complaint arose from the Hellenists against the Hebrews, because their widows were neglected in the daily service.

label: Acts 6:2
text: The twelve summoned the multitude of the disciples and said, “It is not appropriate for us to forsake the word of God and serve tables.

label: Acts 6:3
text: Therefore select from among you, brothers, seven men of good report, full of the Holy Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business.

label: Acts 6:4
text: But we will continue steadfastly in prayer and in the ministry of the word.”

label: Acts 6:5
text: These words pleased the whole multitude. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a proselyte of Antioch;

label: Acts 6:6
text: whom they set before the apostles. When they had prayed, they laid their hands on them.

label: Acts 6:7
text: The word of God increased and the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem exceedingly. A great company of the priests were obedient to the faith.

label: Acts 6:8
text: Stephen, full of faith and power, performed great wonders and signs among the people.

label: Acts 6:9
text: But some of those who were of the synagogue called “The Libertines”, and of the Cyrenians, of the Alexandrians, and of those of Cilicia and Asia arose, disputing with Stephen.

label: Acts 6:10
text: They weren’t able to withstand the wisdom and the Spirit by which he spoke.

label: Acts 6:11
text: Then they secretly induced men to say, “We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses and God.”

label: Acts 6:12
text: They stirred up the people, the elders, and the scribes, and came against him and seized him, and brought him in to the council,

label: Acts 6:13
text: and set up false witnesses who said, “This man never stops speaking blasphemous words against this holy place and the law.

label: Acts 6:14
text: For we have heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place, and will change the customs which Moses delivered to us.”

label: Acts 6:15
text: All who sat in the council, fastening their eyes on him, saw his face like it was the face of an angel.

label: Philip (the evangelist)
note: One of the Seven appointed in Acts 6:5; distinct from Philip the apostle and Philip the Tetrarch.

label: Hellenist (Greek-speaking) Jews lived in Jerusalem
statement: The Jerusalem community included Hellenists (Greek-speaking Jews) as well as Hebrews, and the Hellenist widows were neglected in the daily distribution.
note: The ossuary evidence shows Greek in use among Jerusalem Jews, not a distinct Hellenist faction; the factional split rests on Acts itself.

label: A daily distribution of food was made to widows
statement: The Jerusalem community administered a daily distribution (of food) to its widows.

label: The Twelve appointed seven men, among them Stephen and Philip
statement: The community chose seven men of good report - Stephen, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas and Nicolaus - and the apostles prayed and laid their hands on them (6:5-6).

label: A great company of priests became obedient, and the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem
statement: The word of God increased, the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem exceedingly, and a great company of the priests became obedient to the faith.

label: A Jerusalem synagogue of Libertines (Freedmen), Cyrenians and Alexandrians
statement: There was in Jerusalem a synagogue called that of the Libertines (Freedmen), with Cyrenians, Alexandrians, and people from Cilicia and Asia; some of its members disputed with Stephen.
note: Opinion is divided whether Acts 6:9 names one synagogue or several (Wikipedia, Synagogue of the Libertines). The Greek funerary evidence attests the diaspora communities' presence, not this synagogue's name.

label: Men were induced to accuse Stephen of blasphemy against Moses and God
statement: Opponents secretly induced men to say, 'We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses and God.'

label: Stephen was seized and brought before the council
statement: They stirred up the people, the elders and the scribes, came upon Stephen, seized him and brought him before the council (Sanhedrin).

label: Witnesses charged that Jesus would destroy this place and change the customs of Moses
statement: False witnesses charged that Stephen's hearers had heard him say that Jesus of Nazareth would destroy this place and change the customs which Moses delivered.

label: The council saw Stephen's face like an angel's face
statement: All who sat in the council, fastening their eyes on Stephen, saw his face as it had been the face of an angel.

label: Wikipedia: Synagogue of the Libertines
title: Synagogue of the Libertines
excerpt: In this instance, "libertine" refers to one has been liberated, that is, a former slave or freedman. Those attending this particular synagogue might also include the descendants of such freedmen.

label: Sefaria: Mishnah Peah 8:7 (the charity dish and the communal fund)
title: Mishnah Peah 8:7
excerpt: He who has the money for two meals, he may not take anything from the charity dish. And if he has enough money for fourteen meals, he may not take any support from the communal fund.

label: Wikipedia: Second Temple period (Greek inscriptions on ossuaries)
title: Second Temple period (ossuary inscriptions in Hebrew or Greek)
excerpt: Funerary inscriptions with names etched or inscribed in Hebrew or Greek ossuaries are commonly found on ossuaries and sometimes on tombs.

label: Mishnah Peah 8:7 (the charity dish (tamchuy) and the communal fund (kupah))
author: Mishnah
date: compiled c. 200 CE (material largely Second Temple era)

label: Wikipedia: Theodotos inscription (the Greek text in English translation)
title: Theodotos inscription
excerpt: built the synagogue for the reading of the Law and the teaching of the commandments, as well as the guest-house and the (other) rooms and water installations(?) for the lodging of those who are in need of it from abroad
